subject: Midcycle capacity uplift & co-term alignment for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: midcycle capacity uplift & co-term path for Aurora Health

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the update on last week's usage spike. We saw the telemetry you shared and it looks like production traffic is consistently 2.5x the baseline we patched into the renewal. Congrats on the adoption — happy problem to have.

To keep latency and unit economics predictable for you, I sketched two workable approaches that avoid a long-term double-billing scenario while giving Aurora immediate headroom:

- Option 1 — Annualize now (co-term): Add a midcycle uplift to the existing contract for the incremental capacity (approx. +55% token commitment), effective immediately, then annualize to co-term on your renewal date. We can offer a 15% uplift discount on the incremental commit if Aurora signs the SOW amendment and co-terms now. Proration would be handled on the invoice to reflect the partial period.

- Option 2 — Staged top-up with bridge credit: Immediate top-up to cover current spike (short-term monthly billing) with a bridge credit applied when you co-term at renewal. Bridge credit equals % of the excess paid in the top-up period and converts to commitment credit on signature. This keeps your invoice smaller today and protects you from paying full uplift rates twice. We can propose a 10% staging discount for this path.

Both options include the same performance SLAs for Dedicated throughput and a one-time migration support credit to help with any model pinning you need. Attached is a draft SOW amendment and a redline that shows the billing and proration math.

Can you confirm Aurora's preferred path and the procurement timeline? If you prefer, Ben can run the actual proration numbers against last 90 days of usage and Laura can confirm invoicing cadence.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[t] 415-555-0182
[Attachment: Aurora_Renewal_Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 293KB)]
From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@aurorahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: midcycle capacity uplift & co-term path for Aurora Health

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear options. Short answers: procurement wants the simple math and a single go/no-go by Dec 21 so we can include this in our Q4 financial close. We prefer Option 2 (staged top-up + bridge credit) if the credit is guaranteed and the conversion math is spelled out. Three asks from our side: 

1) Can you show the proration math with our actual usage (Nov 1–Nov 30)?
2) We need the invoice schedule for the staged top-up (monthly? immediate one-time invoice?).
3) Can legal confirm there is no double-charge risk if we co-term later in March?

Cc'ing procurement to keep them in the loop. If procurement is OK with the staged path, they'll want a single consolidated invoice option (one invoice that includes any proration adjustments) rather than multiple micro invoices.

Claire D'Souza
Head of Applied AI, Aurora Health
Claire.Dsouza@aurorahealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@aurorahealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: midcycle capacity uplift & co-term path for Aurora Health

Claire —

Appreciate the timeline. I attached two quick spreadsheets in the redline PDF but here are the practical numbers against Nov usage (rounded):

- Baseline commit: 18M tokens/month
- Observed average Nov: 46M tokens/month (excess 28M)
- Proposed staged top-up: immediate +30M tokens/month for Dec–Feb (covers spike)

Billing options we recommend: 
A) Staged Top-up (monthly invoices): 30M tokens/month at your current hosted rate, billed monthly. When you co-term, bridge credit = total excess paid over baseline (Dec–Feb) × 0.9 (to reflect staged discount) applied to the first invoice after co-term signature.
B) Immediate Annualize (one-time amendment): Add +30M/month to commit, annualize now, 15% discount on the incremental portion; proration applied for the remainder of this contract year.

We believe Option A gives Aurora GA flexibility while protecting you from duplicate payments via the bridge credit. Laura — can you confirm the consolidated invoice approach is straightforward for finance? We can issue one invoice that aggregates Dec usage and a proration line item rather than three small invoices if procurement prefers.

[Attachment: SOW-Amendment.docx (docx, 47KB)]

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@aurorahealth.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@aurorahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: midcycle capacity uplift & co-term path for Aurora Health

Ben/Tessa —

Procurement here. The staged path is acceptable provided the following are in writing:

- Bridge credit formula (we need a worked example).
- Single consolidated invoice option for the staged period (we want one charge per month that includes proration lines, not >3 line items per day).
- Confirmation that bridge credit will appear as a credit memo on our account and reduce future invoices (no refunds).

Worked example request: if Aurora pays 30M tokens for Dec and our renewal co-terms on Mar 15, show how the Dec–Feb payments become credits and what the first post-signature invoice looks like. Also need standard PO fields for the invoice (PO#, bill-to address).

Please include the DocuSign link for the amendment so legal can circulate internally; timeline: procurement review complete by Dec 21, legal sign-off by Jan 8.

procurement@aurorahealth.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 15:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: midcycle capacity uplift & co-term path for Aurora Health

Hi all —

Thanks — we can confirm the staged top-up path with the exact bridge-credit worked example and consolidated invoice. Summary we will publish to the amendment / redline: 

- Staged top-up: +30M tokens/month (Dec–Feb). Invoices: one consolidated invoice per month that includes a proration line for the partial month if needed.
- Bridge credit: 90% of sums paid on staged top-ups converted to commitment credit upon co-term signature. Example (worked): Aurora pays $45,000/month for Dec–Feb = $135,000 total. Upon co-term, $121,500 (90%) is applied as a credit against the new annualized commit; the remaining $13,500 is treated as usage premium for the short-term coverage.
- Credit treatment: credit memo applied to first post-signature invoice (no cash refunds).
- PO & invoice fields: please send PO# and billing address; Laura and our billing team will ensure invoices match your fields.
- Legal/DocuSign: Ben will publish a final amendment with those clauses and the DocuSign link. We can also offer a one-time SLA exception that guarantees Dedicated throughput targets during the staged period.

We will circulate the final amendment and the HubSpot record by EOD Monday so procurement has the DocuSign link to route.

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
